Subject: Dedicated GPU sizing: tiered H100/A100/L4 plan for Meridian Foods

Carlos — thanks for the time today. Following up with a focused sizing note so we can align on a pilot capacity that matches your SLA targets and real traffic shape. I attached the quick profile workbook (meridian_gpu_profile_v1.xlsx) you promised to check and pasted the key asks below.

High-level recommendation preview (so we have a frame for discussion):
- Tiered fleet: L4 for high-volume low-memory/short-turnaround queries, A100 for sustained throughput and medium-context generation, H100 reserved for memory-bound long-context synthesis and retrieval-augmented flows.
- KV-prefix caching and a small L4 edge pool to capture the 60–70% steady-state short requests.
- Reserve a small H100 pool for 99th/long-context tail and cross-region fallback behavior.

What we need from you to finalize numbers:
1) Expected QPS for the first 3 months (peak and baseline).
2) SLA targets: P50/P95/P99 latency goals per endpoint type (chat short vs long context).
3) Percent of requests that use >4k tokens and approximate median token counts for those.
4) Any hard budget ceiling or reserved-commitment preference.

Attachments included: meridian_gpu_profile_v1.xlsx (workbook with sample traces) — please drop your usage export into tab 'prod-sample' if you can.

Next step: if you reply with the numbers below by EOD tomorrow we'll run a quick capacity simulation and propose an initial pilot fleet composition + fallback policy.

Cheers,
Jordan Blake

Baseline QPS: 120 steady, peak single-region burst ~420 QPS (we see this daily at 14:00 ET).
SLA targets:
- Short chat endpoints: P95 <= 220 ms, P99 <= 450 ms.
- Long-context generation (retrieval + summarize): P95 <= 1.2 s, P99 <= 3.5 s.

Token distribution (rough):
- ~68% are short queries (~30–150 tokens).
- ~25% medium (~150–2k tokens).
- ~7% long (>4k tokens), and about 1–1.5% are extreme >20k tokens (monthly spikes).

Budget: we can commit to a pilot reserved pool but need a clear forecast for steady-state hourly cost before any annual committment.

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU sizing: tiered H100/A100/L4 plan for Meridian Foods

Agree with Jordan's tiered approach. Did a quick back-of-envelope run against Carlos's numbers to surface an initial capacity sketch and where tradeoffs live. Notes below — this is intentionally conservative on headroom for the pilot.

Traffic math (baseline numbers):
- Peak QPS: 420; target P95 short latency 220 ms -> average latency short ~120–180 ms, pick 0.18s for concurrency calc.
- Estimated concurrent short requests at peak: 420 * 0.18s ≈ 76 concurrent short requests.
- Medium and long requests drive extra concurrency because of longer token generation. Approx add 30 concurrent slots for medium and 10 for long in steady peak, so total ~116 concurrent active requests at peak.

Model memory and perf assumptions (pilot models):
- L4 (quantized): excellent inference cost per token for short prompts, ~low memory (fits many small models per GPU), fast cold-start. Best for ~70% traffic.
- A100 (40GB): good balance for medium context generation, higher throughput for batching, fits larger FP16 models and moderate KV-cache sizes. Best for ~20% traffic.
- H100 (80GB): needed for heavy retrieval+generate, long-context (>8k), larger KV caches, lower latency for long sequences when not heavily batched. Best for ~10% traffic (but important for tail).

Pilot composition suggestion (initial, before autoscale/burst):
- L4: 20 cards (handles short steady-state; scales horizontally, cheap per-card).
- A100: 6 cards (handles medium/throughput workloads with batching).
- H100: 3 cards (kept warm for long-context paths and as a fallback for degraded A100 capacity).

Rationale: L4 pool sized to absorb 70% of traffic with modest batching; A100/A100s for aggregated medium flows that benefit from batching, H100 reserved for memory headroom and to satisfy P99 on long-context flows. We estimate this mix to meet P95 targets with ~25–35% headroom.

Operational guardrails I recommend:
- KV-prefix caching for high hit-rate queries to reduce H100 pressure.
- Smart routing: route by profile (short/medium/long) with automatic fallback to the next-compatible pool if primary pool is saturated.
- Autoscale thresholds with cold-start buffer for H100 (keep N warm tokens).

I'll run a cost estimate with current Redwood list prices and share a rough delta vs. full H100-only vs L4-heavy options.

—Dev
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU sizing: tiered H100/A100/L4 plan for Meridian Foods

Couple of operational notes to add before we lock numbers:

1) Reserved vs burst mix: Meridian asked for pilot cost predictability. Recommend a small reserved backbone (50–60% of pilot L4 and A100) and maintain burst pools (on-demand) for H100 to avoid paying reserved for infrequent extremes.

2) Quantization / model packing: for L4 we should push INT8/4-bit packing where model quality allows — frees memory to host more replicas and reduces per-token cost. Need Meridian's acceptance criteria on evals for any quantized profile.

3) Fallback and throttling policy: define clear degrade path — short requests should never route to H100 unless A100/L4 are fully saturated; when fallback happens, add request-weighted throttling or lower-generation temperature to preserve latency.

4) Suggested pilot numbers (ops-safe, includes 30% buffer over Dev's conservative calc):
- L4: 26 cards (handles short traffic + headroom)
- A100: 8 cards
- H100: 4 cards (keep 2 warm, 2 can be cold but with fast warm-up)

5) Attach runbook stub and basic checklist for the pilot: health checks, warmup scripts, KV-cache priming, escalation contacts. See operational_runbook_stub.md attached.

If Meridian is comfortable with those numbers we can turn this into a formal pilot proposal and price it. I can draft the runbook if Dev agrees on the routing rules.

—Kimberly Park
Director, Dedicated Operations — Redwood Inference
